newsitem.title: USA: Domestic U.S. crudes attracting stronger Gulf bids.
newsitem.headline: Domestic U.S. crudes attracting stronger Gulf bids.

text.p: U.S. cash crude barrels remained firm Tuesday on tightness in foreign markets, forcing refiners to pay premiums for key domestic grades.
Outright crudes lost ground, however, retreating to slightly weaker levels in a consolidation move after Monday's more than $1.00 run-up.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was pegged around 15 cents lower at $21.20-30 a barrel, with June losing half its premium to the July month to 6-7 cents.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was sold out to a 13 cents premium to June WTI/Cushing, but faded from that level later in the morning, traders said.
West Texas Sour/Midland also gained, selling at a $1.38 discount to the marker, 7-9 cents firmer than Monday.
Markets found support from news of a blast at Citgo Petroleum Corp's 132,500 barrels per day refinery in Corpus Christi, Texas.

Traders said the end to the fishermen's blockade of Britain's Sullom Voe terminal took some edge off the bullish stance for sweets in the Gulf, but underlying fundamentals remained a positive factor for the LLS and Midland markets.
Exchange for physicals (EFP's) were talked at a strong plus 10-12 cents level this morning, continuing a trend favoring WTI/Cushing ahead of June futures expiry.
June WTI/Cushing Postings Plus retreated with the decline in June/July spreads, selling most recently at $2.06, from $2.19 on Monday.
